question.leadin: Popular protest slogans during this time period often started with "Ash-shab yurid," meaning "the people want."
question.text: Name this series of political movements in North Africa and the Middle East that began in December 2010.
question.clue: One government destroyed the Pearl Roundabout, a gathering place for protests during this period.

swap.leadin: Under the grip of its fifth president, this country was in turmoil beginning in 1980 and culminating in 2003 when it was invaded by a "coalition of the willing."
swap.text: Name this Middle Eastern country established by the British in 1921. The first ruler of this country was the Hashemite king Faisal I.
swap.answerHtml: Iraq (or Republic of Iraq or Jumhuriyat al- Iraq )
swap.clue: One autonomous region in this country was the location of a civil war between two rival political dynasties, one of which rules that region today.

question.text: After France was granted control of the Levant in the end of World War I, the Hashemites established an Arab Kingdom in this country and unsuccessfully fought the French. Today, this country is controversially led by Bashar al-Assad.
question.clue: Odaenathus ruled a city in this country that fought against Aurelian under its queen Zenobia, Palmyra.

swap.text: The First Crusade ended when Christian soldiers captured and massacred the defenders of this city. Saladin's reconquest of this city in 1187 sparked the Third Crusade.
swap.clue: The Irgun, without the approval of the Haganah paramilitary, bombed this city's King David Hotel.

question.leadin: Tariq ibn Ziyad, who served this dynasty, conquered the Iberian Peninsula from the Visigoths.
question.text: Name this caliphate based in Damascus which conquered large swaths of territory in Central Asia and Southwestern Europe.
question.clue: This empire rose to power after their victory in a conflict sparked by the killing of Uthman ibn Affan.

swap.leadin: Name these places where archaeological discoveries were announced in 2022.
swap.text: An ivory comb bearing an ancient Canaanite (KAY-nuh-nyte) engraving was unearthed at Tel Lachish (TEL lah-KEESH) in this country. The mountaintop fortress of Masada (muh-SAH-dah) is also in this country.
swap.clue: Along with Lehi , another paramilitary group carried out the Deir Yassin massacre in this modern-day country, although the Haganah criticized them for violating this country's "purity of arms" policy.

question.leadin: Answer some things about the exploits of Nazi special forces commander, Otto Skorzeny: ["Score-zeh-nee"].
question.text: After the war, Skorzeny served as a military advisor to this leader. Anthony Eden resigned as British Prime Minister after failing to dislodge this leader in the Suez Crisis.
question.clue: As part of one conflict, he blockaded Eilat under the suggestion of his defense minister Amer.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about genocide reprisals.
swap.text: One employee of this agency, Zvi Aharoni, identified "Ricardo Klement" as the Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann, after which this agency captured and smuggled him out of Argentina to face trial and execution.
swap.clue: This agency undertook an extrajudicial operation which captured and led to the execution of Adolf Eichmann after he was discovered hiding in Argentina.

question.text: Known on both sides for the holidays on which it started, this 1973 attack by Egypt and Syria led to the OPEC embargo.
question.answerHtml: Yom Kippur War [or Ramadan War; prompt on October War]
question.clue: Before this conflict, Henry Kissinger advised Golda Meir not to launch a pre-emptive attack.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about sectarian violence in a certain Middle Eastern country.
swap.text: Martial law was declared in Syria in expectation of mass rioting in the wake of this 1956 event, which saw Britain, France, and Israel launch an attack in response to the nationalization of the namesake Egyptian canal.
swap.answerHtml: the Suez Crisis [or the Tripartite Aggression; or Operation Kadesh; or the Sinai War]
swap.clue: Robert Menzies failed to end this event peacefully, leading to the bombing of troops under Abdel Hakim Amer in this event's Operation Musketeer.

question.text: The Marinid promotion of learning allowed them to briefly patronise this Tunis-born scholar, the author of the Muqaddimah ("moo-KAHD-ee-mah") who is sometimes cited as the father of sociology.
question.clue: This thinker, a longtime judge in Cairo, was a strong proponent of the concept of assabiya, or social solidarity.

swap.leadin: During this war, humans surrendered to a drone for the first time in human history.
swap.text: Name this war that also saw the final deployment of battleships in a combat role. The losing side in this war set fire to the oil wells of a nation that had earlier been accused of slant drilling.
swap.clue: A Las Vegas conference in this war's aftermath led to the Tailhook sexual assault scandal.

question.text: This caliph sent the general Amr ibn al-'As to capture that fortress at Babylon, whereupon he founded Fustat. This caliph, who succeeded Abu Bakr and preceded Uthman, was given the title al-Farooq by Muhammad.
question.clue: The last Sassanian king, Yazdegird III, was murdered by a brigand after his forces were defeated by this caliph's force at Qadisiyya. His creation of the qadi judgeship and divan pension system is considered the beginning of Islamic jurisprudence.

swap.text: Fatimah, the daughter of this Sunni theologian, is also known for her dedication to women's education as part of Islamic reform. This theologian founded a namesake religious movement adopted by Muhammad bin Saud.
swap.answerHtml: Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhāb [or Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhāb ibn Sulaymān al-Tamīmī; accept Wahhabi movement or Wahhabism or Wahhabiyya]
swap.clue: In his hometown of Uyaynah, he gained the favor of a ruler named Uthman, whom he directed to begin a campaign of iconoclasm, destroying the domes on the gravesites of Muhammad's companion.

question.leadin: A 1744 marriage alliance between the families of an emir and a religious reformer formed the cultural basis for this state in its attempt to unify Arabia.
question.text: Name this state based in Nejd whose conservative interpretation of Islam was marked by desecration of tombs and expansion of the Hanbali school of jurisprudence.
question.answerHtml: Emirate of Diriyah [or First Saudi State; prompt on Saudi State; reject “Saudi Arabia”] (The emir was Muhammad bin Saud and the religion reformer was Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab.)
question.clue: After he established control over Egypt, Muhammad Ali conquered this Arabic state. This state was founded by Muhammad Ibn Saud and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, the founders of the Saud dynasty and Wahhabism, respectively.

swap.leadin: This man attempted to catch a pair of shoes thrown at George W. Bush during a press conference.
swap.text: Name this former Prime Minister of Iraq whose accession was brokered by Qasem Soleimani as a compromise between Kurds and Shi'ites.

question.leadin: Answer stuf about capital cities during the Abbasid Dynasty.
question.text: For twelve years under al-Hasan, this city was the frst Abbasid capital. The caliph Ali had been assassinated with a poison sword while praying in the great mosque at this city, which became a center of Islamic theology, and lends its name to the earliest style of handwritten script used to record the Quran.
question.clue: As a leader of this city knelt to begin the morning prayer in its Great Mosque, he was struck with a poisoned sword by a Kharijite.

swap.text: During Poland's 1968 crisis, a government campaign nominally targeting this ideology resulted in the expulsion of two-thirds of Poland's Jews. Theodor Herzl created a "congress" for this ideology in 1897.
swap.clue: That letter supporting this cause was written by Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour.

question.leadin: This mystic famously declared "I am the Truth," prompting allegations that he claimed to be divine.
question.text: Name this mystic who was crucified by the Abbasid Caliph Al-Muqtadir in 922.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the assassinations of some 20th Century Middle Eastern leaders, FTPE.
swap.text: The son of the Kataeb Party's founder, this man organized and commanded the Lebanese Forces to combat Syrian occupation. Elected as Lebanon's president in 1982, he was killed in a bomb blast before he could take office, and his brother Amine was elected as his replacement.
swap.clue: This leader of the Phalangist Party, who united the Maronite militias of Lebanon. His party emerged victorious from the 1982 Lebanon War with Israeli support and the expulsion of the PLO.
